citations.review_text: Unlike the other Telltale games, this game retells the characters of some well-known fairy tales in a completely different and quite refreshing way in a gritty, dark, and at times rather depressing crime thriller for adults, in which beloved characters like Belle, Ichabold Crane, and Snow White struggle for survival and their pride in a story revolving around murder, prostitution, and violence. Once you get used to it, this story definitely develops a certain pull. Wrapped in a twisty crime story that constantly throws curveballs, you definitely stay engaged, even if the Telltale team isn't quite as dramatically sophisticated as in their best work. Despite its relatively short runtime, there are a few lulls: the story is bogged down by some dispensable elements. Subplots like the one involving Belle and the Beast are unnecessarily inflated, and the initially spectacularly introduced but later forgotten secondary antagonist, Bluebeard, seems to have been left hanging in the narrative. Several questions remain unsatisfactorily unanswered until the very end. For example, the whereabouts of an initial suspect who suddenly vanishes from the story without much fanfare. Overall, the story feels somewhat unfocused at times, focusing on too many characters who are simply forgotten over time. The central characters, however, are significantly better and more coherently written, experiencing several pivotal moments and undergoing believable development. The action sequences are also exceptionally well-executed this time around, featuring several brutal spectacles. It's also a great pleasure that the game runs flawlessly from a technical standpoint, which is exceptional for Telltale adventures: no crashes, no visual glitches, and no sound bugs. This greatly enhances the enjoyment of the game and ensures a smooth and satisfying experience. Then, the story picks up pace as it builds momentum, building from its occasional slow moments to a mostly coherent and pleasantly atmospheri…

citations.review_text:
This game is absolutely fantastic. I went into it expecting a good story, but I honestly didn’t expect to get this invested this quickly, as I lose interest after a couple of hours. The atmosphere, characters, dialogue, and overall noir/fairytale setting are absolutely incredible.

Great protagonist, and the way the game slowly reveals more about Fabletown makes every conversation feel important. I especially love how the choices actually make you stop and think about what kind of person you want to be. Even seemingly small decisions feel like they could come back to matter later.

The art style and soundtrack fit perfectly too. There’s something about the dark, gritty atmosphere mixed with these familiar fairytale characters that works ridiculously well.

I’m only two episodes in, so I’m genuinely excited to see where the story goes. If the rest of the game keeps this level of writing and atmosphere, I can already tell this is going to be one of those games I’ll remember for a long time. So hella exited for the sequel also!!

10/10 so far.

The Wolf Among Us is one of those games that completely pulled me into its story. The story-driven action, mystery, characters, and overall atmosphere were absolutely amazing.

One of my favorite things about the game was the mystery. From the beginning, you're constantly trying to figure out what's actually happening and who you can trust. Every clue, conversation, and decision makes you want to keep playing because you want to know what happens next.

The story is also really well written. Playing as Bigby Wolf and investigating the strange events happening in Fabletown made the whole game feel like you were actually part of a detective story. The characters are interesting, and the relationships between them make the decisions feel like they actually matter.

I also really enjoyed the action. Even though it's primarily a story-driven game, the action scenes are intense and do a great job breaking up the investigation and dialogue. The choices you make throughout the game also make you feel like you're shaping your own version of the story.

The art style is another thing that makes the game stand out. It has a comic-book look that fits the world perfectly and gives it its own identity.

Overall, I thought The Wolf Among Us was an amazing experience. The mystery kept me interested, the story was fantastic, the characters were memorable, and the combination of investigation, choices, and action made it really fun to play.

It is with a heavy heart that I do not recommend this game. Sigh.

I really wanted to like everything, but I couldn't. 

Story started great, but the pacing sucked. Going the paragon route also glossed over some choices + consequences. The ending is pretty anti-climactic (they shouldn't have dragged it out for a fifth chapter and should've just fleshed out the fourth one).

[strike]I... might replay the game and do a renegade run. And I will probably update this review afterwards if I find a significant difference with story quality. [/strike] Edit: Replaying did not make a significant difference to the pacing and the ending.

Also, the QTE is pretty heavy on this telltale. This is my 2nd one, after Tales from the Borderlands. Considering that Tales from the Borderlands was a newer release, the QTE/story execution was so much better there. For Wolf, if I wanted this much QTE, I would just be playing OSU!... I'm exaggerating, but I personally think it just doesn't work for this game.

Nonetheless, the characters are great. The atmosphere as well. The art style is amazing and really succeeds at giving off a comic-book vibe. The music is pretty iconic for the game as well. The game lacks recent telltale QoL features but it's not the worst.

Telltale Games reached a phenomenal high-water mark with The Wolf Among Us, delivering a dark, neo-noir detective thriller that takes classic fairytale characters and drops them into a gritty, 1980s New York enclave known as Fabletown. Stepping into the shoes of Bigby Wolf the reformed Big Bad Wolf turned Sheriff you're thrust into a murder investigation that pulls back the curtain on a corrupt, desperate underworld filled with familiar folklore figures struggling just to get by.

What truly carries the game is its unbelievable atmosphere and style. The vibrant neon-and-ink cel-shaded visual aesthetic, combined with a incredible synth-heavy soundtrack, creates a immersive noir vibe from start to finish. The writing is sharp, mature, and punchy, offering a refreshing take on characters like Snow White, Mr. Toad, and Bigby himself. The tension between controlling Bigby's violent monster side versus keeping your cool during intense interrogations leads to some of the most satisfying moral choices Telltale has ever designed.

It isn't quite a perfect score due to a few classic Telltale quirks a couple of minor pacing dips mid-season and moments where choices feel more like the illusion of control rather than branching paths. However, the sheer strength of its mystery, brilliant voice performances, and incredible aesthetic make it a standout narrative adventure. An absolute must-play for fans of mystery, noir, and story-driven games.

Score: 8.5/10

Imagine taking classic fairy tale characters, throwing them into the grim, drug fueled backdrop of 1980s New York, and forcing them to hide among humans using black market magic. You’re Bigby Wolf, formerly the Big Bad Wolf working as the local sheriff. Everyone hates you for your violent past, but when a gruesome murder hits the district, you’re the only one who can crack the case before the whole secret community tears itself apart.

The neon-synth aesthetic and comic book art style are incredible. Bigby is an awesome protagonist, and you spend the whole game deciding whether to be a decent lawman or just go full monster when people push you. It takes a crazy concept and turns it into a genuinely dark story about crime and corruption.

It’s classic Telltale, so "gameplay" is mostly picking dialogue under a timer and mashing keys during action scenes. Your choices shape how characters view you rather than completely changing the ending, but the story is so good you won't care.

It's stylish, tense, and effortlessly cool from start to finish. Grab a drink, turn off the lights, and just let it ride.

citations.review_text: The Wolf Among Us is a representation of the best Telltale games has to offer. The game is a highly worthy adaptation of the Fable comic series and takes the aspects of what makes that series great and translates it well into a game format, in typical Telltale games fashion. The gameplay is nothing special or innovative (typical Telltale QTE format) but it does strike a good balance between Quick Time events (QTEs) and regular exploration. Uncovering the mystery of the Crooked Man murders proves to make an engaging story with the characters being especially notable. The characters are what makes the typical noir detective story into something truly great with Bigby Wolf, Snow White, and the Crooked Man being the standouts in an already amazing lineup. The voice acting and dialogue is also very well done in this game. Bigby's character arc and how your gameplay choices directly impact his arc are nothing short of peak storytelling and represent major game choices actually having a tangible impact on the story. I'd personally give this game a 9/10.

It is with a heavy heart that I do not recommend this game. Sigh.

citations.review_text: Game is ok, but the characters felt flat and the story did too. Ran into bugs every now and then, with choices breaking at the start of every new chapter. Also hate that you can't skip the recap and the next episode preview. Can't really see the hype tbh, go get Dispatch instead.

This game was a blast to play! Great artstyle, voice acting, character design, story. Magnifique, I tell you. Some minor downsides were that moving and the changing camera angles when moving were slightly janky, and that the intro sequence and credits rolled for every episode. Play this game if you want to be wowed like I was.

I generally recommend this game for exciting story & characters. I was also impressed with the whole artwork. Controls are straight forward.

Things I wish somebody told me before:

1. Lengthy Unskippable Dialogs
The game is all about choices. You can't easily go back and chose a different response or action without having to go through all the dialog again up until the point. The sooner you accept that and learn to live with choices, even bad ones, the better your experience will become. I still wish there was an option to skip dialogs.

2. Mandator Response Countdown
I am a slow reader and the response countdowns generally just ruin the flow for me. They can't be disabled or made last longer. They can be cheated by pausing the game which is a bit annoying but an acceptable workaround for me.

3. Actions After Lengthy Dialog
You need to be awake. There can be minutes of dialog talking you to sleep when you're already tired and then suddenly you have to act withing a time limit of 1-2 seconds.

4. Generally Spoken, Everthing Will Be Fine
It may often feel like you lost or were too slow to act. But the general outcome is usually determined beforehands, so don't worry too much, just continue the game. Details may be affected, but rarely the mainline story.

With that in mind and mainly just enjoying the story, it was a great game and I heard a sequel is on its way. Looking forward to that!

citations.review_text: It was a wonderful experience to play! Took me about almost 27 hours to complete the game! I already am a sucker for fairy tales so playing as one was even more eye opening that I anticipated! One thing I will say is during my first playthrough, I experienced some bugs such as Bigby not holding a specific item I collected or some random item popping in when I grabbed a different item. Apart from slight bugs that are easily fixable by going in and out of the game or restarting it from the last save point (or boldy just following through), it told an amazing story as the good sheriff, someone who's trying to just make it through the day, or the bad guy (which personally hurt me a bit in my lil heart), the player will enjoy the story unfolding in front of them! No matter what role they play! I'm personally excited to see the remastered version and the wolf among us 2! I just hope that the next time when I'm giving someone money, I don't accidentally give them a glass in the future :3

8/10 The Wolf Among Us is a narrative game with limited choices and a great story. Clever, gritty, and highly entertaining.

The Wolf Among Us is an interactive narrative driven adventure game where your choices matter and drastically change the outcome of your story. You play as Bigby, better known as The Big Bad Wolf, a detective who’s tasked with solving crimes committed by various fairytale characters in a gritty, offbeat, and extremely clever rendition.

The gameplay is what you’d expect from a Telltale game- lots of cutscenes with choices that shape your story. After playing a few times I was impressed with the amount of detail that went into the narrative and the small subtle differences that came from making different choices. The artstyle is perfect for the subject and I thought the sound effects, dialogue, music, and voice acting added a lot to the game. I encountered no bugs while playing and the game ran smoothly.

It took me ~80 hours to finish the game in its entirety with all achievements. No trading cards.

Although the game presents you with choices, the way they affect the overarching story is limited. Many of the choices lead to the same result and although there’s minor difference nearly everyone who plays will reach the same conclusions which is a bit disappointing for an otherwise great choice based narrative game. The quick time events are hard to miss which makes the game feel easy and not very interactive.

The story alone makes The Wolf Among Us worth it but it doesn’t deliver a true choice base experience.
